mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or GDP growth is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate increases borrowing and spending, stimulating economic growth and leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 0.1 (t-test p > 0.05), or the federal funds rate is not negatively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 5 (t-test p > 0.05), or the unemployment rate is not negatively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production growth is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing, leading to increased economic activity and higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are above 1200 (t-test p > 0.05), or housing starts are not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low inflation and low interest rates indicates a favorable monetary environment, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low inflation and low interest rates (t-test p > 0.05), or the combination of low inflation and low interest rates is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low unemployment and high payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05), or the combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in retail sales indicates increased consumer spending, leading to increased economic activity and higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during periods of monetary easing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of monetary easing and rising retail sales (t-test p > 0.05), or retail sales growth is not positively correlated with stock prices during monetary easing periods.
